posts.title: The coordinator now writes here
posts.summary: From today the morning briefs, evening check-ins, Sunday reviews, current-affairs notes and deadline alarms are published in this notebook instead of being sent as chat messages.

posts.title: Day 12, Friday 16 October
posts.summary: 219 days to go. The last weekday of the re-cut week: Articles 23 to 35 and the Directive Principles after the carry-forward. Two new Ramsar sites and the September labour-force numbers.

posts.title: Eleven days, one weekday left in Week 2
posts.summary: Day 11 unlogged. Four of the five weekdays of the re-cut week are gone.

posts.title: Day 11, Thursday 15 October
posts.summary: 220 days to go. Chapters 1 to 6 carried forward, then Fundamental Rights, Articles 12 to 22. The Cabinet renewed the National Social Assistance Programme and cleared the IDBI sale.

posts.title: Ten days
posts.summary: Day 10 unlogged. Three of Week 2's weekdays gone; six chapters carried.

posts.title: Day 10, Wednesday 14 October
posts.summary: 221 days to go. Chapters 1 to 4 carried forward, then the Union, its territory and citizenship. BIMSTEC's Delhi Declaration and five years of GatiShakti.

posts.title: Nine days, two of Week 2's weekdays gone
posts.summary: Day 9 unlogged. If the week ends at zero, Sunday 18 October cuts the plan to the real hours.

posts.title: Day 9, Tuesday 13 October
posts.summary: 222 days to go. Chapters 1 and 2 carried forward, then the salient features and the Preamble. Pulses mission and a new naval craft in the news.

posts.title: Re-cut Week 2 starts the same way
posts.summary: Day 8, the first day of the re-cut week, was not logged. Eight days at zero.

posts.title: Day 8, Monday 12 October
posts.summary: 223 days to go. First day of the re-cut Week 2: Laxmikanth chapters 1 and 2 again, 10 PYQs, and the CSAT diagnostic still open from the weekend.

posts.title: Week 1 closes at zero
posts.summary: Day 7 unlogged. The re-cut from this morning's review holds only if the hours are real.

posts.title: Week 1 scored zero, Week 2 is re-cut
posts.summary: No log on any of the seven days. Week 1's content moves whole into Week 2 with no hours added; the Week 11 buffer is dropped and Ancient, Medieval and Art and Culture shrink to one weekend.

posts.title: Day 7, Sunday 11 October
posts.summary: 224 days to go. Review day: the 25-question Polity test, the error review, and the CSAT diagnostic if it did not happen yesterday.

posts.title: Six days, including the diagnostic day
posts.summary: Saturday was not logged either. The diagnostic, Spectrum chapters 1 to 3 and all of Week 1's Polity carry into Sunday.

posts.title: Day 6, Saturday 10 October
posts.summary: 225 days to go. Spectrum chapters 1 to 3, the CSAT diagnostic on the 2024 paper, 20 PYQs. All of Week 1's Polity is still open.

posts.title: Every weekday of Week 1 is gone
posts.summary: Day 5 unlogged. All of Week 1's Polity is now in the carry-forward. Saturday's diagnostic happens regardless.

posts.title: Day 5, Friday 9 October
posts.summary: 226 days to go. Four days unlogged. Articles 23 to 35 and the Directive Principles close Week 1's Polity; the weekend tests are tomorrow and Sunday.

posts.title: Four days, and the weekend tests are close
posts.summary: Day 4 unlogged. The CSAT diagnostic is on Saturday and the Polity test on Sunday, with no Polity read yet.

posts.title: Day 4, Thursday 8 October
posts.summary: 227 days to go. Three days unlogged. Fundamental Rights, Articles 12 to 22, after the carry-forward. The RBI raised the repo rate.

posts.title: Three days in a row at zero
posts.summary: Days 1 to 3 are all unlogged. Six chapters carried forward. The question now is what is blocking the two-hour slot.

posts.title: Day 3, Wednesday 7 October
posts.summary: 228 days to go. Two days unlogged, so chapters 1 to 4 come before chapters 5 and 6. The RBI rate decision is due today.

posts.title: Two days, no hours recorded
posts.summary: Days 1 and 2 are both unlogged. Four chapters are now in the carry-forward.

posts.title: Day 2, Tuesday 6 October
posts.summary: 229 days to go. Yesterday was not logged, so chapters 1 and 2 come first, then chapters 3 and 4. Three current-affairs items, one unverified.

posts.title: Day 1 was not logged
posts.summary: No log came in for Day 1. Tomorrow's brief will treat today's chapters as unread.

posts.title: Day 1, Monday 5 October
posts.summary: 230 days to go. Nothing to revise yet. Laxmikanth chapters 1 and 2, 10 Polity PYQs, and three items from yesterday's releases.

posts.title: Day 0 review, nothing to score yet
posts.summary: The first Sunday review ran on the day the plan was written. 231 days to go, phase Build, Week 1 fixed chapter by chapter, no deadlines in the next 30 days.

posts.title: Two GitHub repositories, one kept
posts.summary: An audit of two study-resource repos you shared on Day 0. The official PYQ scans are adopted as the question base; the notes repo is a link dump and is skipped.

posts.title: The Prelims 2027 master plan
posts.summary: 231 days, roughly 660 study hours, zero starting base, a full-time job. What gets full depth, what gets cut, and the dates that cannot slip.

posts.title: Current affairs, October 2026
posts.summary: Running note for the month. One line per item: the item, the static syllabus anchor it attaches to, the primary source, and whether a primary source confirmed it.
